newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Stable with active bids and offers.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Stable with active bids and offers.

text.p: Singapore's high sulphur fuel oil market was stable but bids and offers were active and some traders said sentiment had improved slightly from last week's dull trade.
The 180-cst grade was heard traded at $98.50 per tonne and the 380-cst was at $91.00 per tonne, both for May 24-28 lifting, traders said.
Some sellers lowered their offers slightly amid weaker crude values and traders said sufficient supplies might continue adding pressure to prices while demand was lacklustre.
At the end of last week, the 180-cst grade was offered at $98.50/$99.50 per tonne against a bid at $97.50. Only one cargo was traded last week at $100.00 per tonne last Monday.
"Sentiment is improved but supplies are coming in and demand remains thin, which should add pressure to prices," said one trader.
Routine cargoes are coming in from the Middle East but demand is thin and the active gas oil market is expected to continue attracting most trading interest on the Singapore market, traders said.
On SIMEX fuel oil futures contract, sentiment was sluggish with 31 lots traded, with June last edging 30 cents up to $98.10 and July sliding 20 cents to $97.80.
In the LSWR market, Indonesia's Pertamina is heard to allocate at least 3.6 million barrels in May, with another 500,000 barrels rolled over from April, traders said.
However, demand remains slack and traders did not expect prices to pick up soon.
"I think the bearish sentiment will last until June when Japan picks up its summer demand," one trader said.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
